newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City 1997 budget up 22 pct over 1996.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City 1997 budget up 22 pct over 1996.

text.p: The 1997 budget for Mexico City's Federal District will be 37.055 billion pesos, up 22 percent from 1996, the Mexico City finance minister told city legislators in an annual report.
Javier Beristain, finance minister of Mexico City's Federal District, presented the report on Wednesday to the Federal District's Assembly of Representatives.
The Federal District, with a population of 8.5 million, includes the core of Mexico's capital, which is home to the federal government.
Greater Mexico City, with a population of about 16 million, includes part of the state of Mexico, which sprawls around the Federal District to the north, east and west.
"The budget of the Federal District for 1997 will reach 37.055 billion pesos, a figure 22 percent higher with respect to the budget of 1996," a Federal District finance ministry report said.

But the increase falls short of 1996 inflation, which was 27.7 percent nationwide. Officials said the city government would continue its "restrictive spending growth policy" for nonessential programs in 1997.
"Spending will have a social orientation as the city government will deliver more and better services to increase daily spending per family to close to 50 pesos," the report said.
Spending of 47.2 pesos per family in 1997 is up from 39.2 pesos per family in 1996 and 14.4 pesos per family in 1991, the report said.

Transport will receive the largest portion of the 1997 budget at 20 percent, followed by justice and security with 19 percent, social welfare with 16.2 percent, urban infrastructure with 16.1 percent, administration 13.3 percent, debt interest 7.3 percent, environment 7.1 percent and economic development one percent.

Of the city's income, 43 percent comes from its own sources such as property taxes, income tax and other fees; 30.2 percent comes from the federal government; 16.1 percent from borrowing; and 9.4 percent from other sources.
